newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Gaddum - No automatic ECB credit for EMU outs.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Gaddum - No automatic ECB credit for EMU outs.

text.p: Bundesbank vice-president Johann Wilhelm Gaddum on Saturday repeated that European Union states outside the future currency union should not have automatic access to European central bank intraday credits.

"Even if cross-border payments with other central banks and other large banks are opened through Target (the future settlement system), this cannot mean that they have automatic access to a credit line from the ECB," Gaddum said.
Gaddum was addressing a conference of bankers and businessmen in Athens. A copy of his speech was made available in advance in Frankfurt.

The Bundesbank has frequently opposed recent demands that central banks of countries outside the planned monetary union should have the same access to the Target system as the banks of monetary union members.

Gaddum also said it was possible that banks would be allowed to use a broader range of securities, such as loans, to underly their refinancing needs via repurchase agreements once the European Central Bank starts its operations.

"Banks would be enabled to spare highly liquid securities for their commercial trading business and use their more illiquid .. assets to access central bank money in the context of open market activities," he said.
